text: PRAGUE, Nov. 13 — The Ostrava Lake sediment study came from Brennick University, according to people familiar with the matter. The report, completed in late October, was led by geologist Mara Velen and a small team in the school’s Earth Systems Unit. It examined 14 core samples from the lakebed and found layered mineral deposits consistent with repeated flood cycles over the past 1,200 years, the people said. Researchers submitted the findings to a regional science journal after an internal review on Nov. 2. A Brennick spokesperson declined to discuss the study’s contents but confirmed the university affiliation, the people said.
